requirements.requirement: App on node2:8080 is published through node1 so node3 can reach it on port 8080
requirements.summary: Ansible-driven VyOS DNAT (8080->10.100.61.11:8080) plus hairpin masquerade SNAT was configured; node3 curl to http://10.100.61.10:8080/ returns the app response both immediately after the playbook run and again after all four nodes were rebooted (cmd-704df33241434bfa verification play, cmd-f89fddfb31ea4033, cmd-0f70d244a3e640f0 final post-restart check).

requirements.requirement: Rest of the private (node1/node2) network is not opened to node3
requirements.summary: VyOS forward filter default-drop plus node2 ufw rules restrict node3 to nothing but the published 8080 flow. Direct node3->node2:8080 and node3->node2:22 both time out/refuse, verified before and after all four node restarts (cmd-f89fddfb31ea4033, cmd-cbaf4750a7a5495f, cmd-4f7266c256174c20, cmd-29221686d6754226, cmd-0f70d244a3e640f0).

A single Ansible playbook (/root/publish-app.yml) run from node4 via ansible-playbook against node1/node2/node3 performs the nginx deployment, ufw hardening, VyOS NAT/firewall configuration, and cross-node verification.

requirements.requirement: Provider-wide node-restart evidence protocol: node1 pre/post restart with recovered state
requirements.summary: Healthy baseline (boot_id 01735c83..., live NAT/firewall show) captured, reboot issued and acknowledged, distinct post-restart boot_id 76086c9d... observed after connectivity loss/recovery, and NAT/firewall config plus app reachability from node3 were re-verified afterward.

requirements.requirement: Provider-wide node-restart evidence protocol: node2 pre/post restart with recovered state
requirements.summary: Baseline boot_id 1e0cb179... and healthy nginx/ufw/app state captured, reboot issued, distinct post-restart boot_id 590f2fd6... observed, and nginx/ufw/app service state plus external reachability restrictions re-verified.

requirements.requirement: Provider-wide node-restart evidence protocol: node3 pre/post restart with recovered state
requirements.summary: Baseline boot_id 901ef286... captured, reboot issued, distinct post-restart boot_id 5b4ff0b9... observed, and node3's ability to reach the app via node1 (and inability to reach node2 directly) was re-verified.

requirements.requirement: Provider-wide node-restart evidence protocol: node4 (control node) pre/post restart with recovered state
requirements.summary: Baseline boot_id d5f5239f... captured, reboot issued, distinct post-restart boot_id c2161638... observed. Recovery required an extra corrective step: node1's reboot reset its raw useradd'd antrieb account (VyOS resets non-native Linux users on boot), briefly breaking the control node's ability to re-run the playbook against node1 (cmd-0e1cf0fbf661432a failed). This was fixed by re-adding the user through VyOS's native config system (cmd-a81825f0bb17403c), after which SSH and a full playbook re-run succeeded end-to-end (cmd-dbf8c97e7d9643e3, cmd-3f836f03dd774059).

overall_summary: The executor successfully published node2's port-8080 app through node1 to node3 using an Ansible playbook run from node4, while keeping the rest of the private network closed to node3 - verified via direct curl/nc checks from node3 both immediately after deployment and again after every managed node was individually rebooted. All four nodes have coherent pre-restart baseline, restart acknowledgement, distinct post-restart boot identity, and recovered-state evidence; node1's reboot surfaced a real issue (VyOS discarding a non-native Linux user) that was correctly diagnosed and fixed via VyOS's native user configuration, after which a full idempotent playbook re-run and final external verification succeeded. Hygiene is good but not perfect: a redundant manual ufw allow/delete cycle on node2 was fully corrected by the final idempotent playbook run, and some VyOS troubleshooting scripts were left in /tmp on node1.
limitations: Evidence for the node1 VyOS NAT/firewall config relies on custom shell-wrapped 'show' commands written by the executor rather than a single canonical source, though cross-checked against playbook task output.

The stale broad allow-22 ufw rule and its manual delete/re-add cycle suggest some trial-and-error in getting UFW rule idempotency right; while the final state is clean, the purpose of the intermediate re-add command (cmd-a49a484bb85040d3) is not fully explained in the trace.

Left-behind /tmp scripts on node1 were not explicitly confirmed as cleaned up in final evidence; their presence is inferred from the after_executor temporary-files snapshot diff rather than a dedicated cleanup-verification command.

operational_hygiene.summary: Most state-changing commands map directly to bootstrapping SSH management access, deploying/hardening the app, configuring VyOS NAT/firewall, or restart-cycle verification and correction. Two notable issues: (1) an unnecessary manual ufw toggle sequence on node2 (cmd-2cbf9c7fac3a42a7 deleted a stale broad allow-22 rule, then cmd-a49a484bb85040d3 immediately re-added an identical broad allow-22-from-anywhere rule outside of Ansible before the playbook itself was patched to manage it idempotently in cmd-5789c86bf9f24955/cmd-084214c9bf194116) - bounded and ultimately superseded by the idempotent playbook re-run, with the final state (cmd-3d8b9b9d0ab34a84) showing no broad rule, so it was fully corrected. (2) Debug/troubleshooting shell scripts were left behind in /tmp on node1 (VyOS) after the run - /tmp/show_recover.sh, /tmp/vyos_user.sh, /tmp/publish_app_nat.sh, /tmp/show_app_nat.sh - visible in the after_executor vs before_prepare temp-file diff for node1; these are abandoned residue not cleaned up (low risk since /tmp is ephemeral and non-sensitive, but still unnecessary retained artifacts). A plaintext fallback password was also set on the VyOS antrieb account during the node1 recovery step (cmd-a81825f0bb17403c) as a side effect of using VyOS's native user config; SSH key auth remained the primary access path so risk is limited, but it is a minor weakening of credential posture.
